clue.text: Beloved disciple's pain St Peter fails to comprehend

indicators.note: to comprehend is to take in or contain, so one piece is put inside the other
a plan that fails falls apart, so the saint's name is broken up and rearranged

parts.note: an ache is a dull pain

explanation.surface: Biblical scene: St Peter cannot understand the suffering of the disciple Jesus loved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fails' rearranges ST PETER into TERSPET; 'to comprehend' puts ACHE inside it after the first two letters. The 's after 'disciple' stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A teacher's favourite pupil is a much-loved follower, a favoured disciple in a classroom sense.

clue.text: Recognise St Thomas and be pleased — you're improving

parts.note: identifying the saint as Sir Thomas More, Henry VIII's chancellor, you would say 'that's More'
to be pleased with something is to like it

explanation.surface: Someone spots a statue of St Thomas and is delighted with a pupil's progress.
explanation.walkthrough: St Thomas More was the Tudor statesman executed by Henry VIII and later canonised; naming him gives the first two words.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an approving remark made when someone's performance gets better.

clue.text: Ornamental frame chipped on both sides in lumber room, perhaps

indicators.note: chipping a piece off each edge removes the first and last letters of the frame word

parts.note: a lattice is a decorative framework of crossed strips

explanation.surface: A decorative picture frame, damaged at the edges, is stored away in a junk room.
explanation.definitionFit: A loft under the roof is often where old furniture and junk are stored, so it may serve as a lumber room.

clue.text: Announce that woman's clothing is covered in hair

indicators.note: to announce something is to say it out loud, so the phrase is heard rather than read

parts.note: her suit is the clothing belonging to that woman

explanation.surface: A report that a woman's outfit is coated with hairs.
explanation.definitionFit: Hairy and shaggy are synonyms: the word describes a body thickly grown with hair.

clue.text: Relax, employing muscle to get deference

indicators.note: employing something means taking it on, so the relaxing word holds the muscle inside it

parts.note: to relax is to rest
pec is short for pectoral, a chest muscle

explanation.surface: Advice to unwind while using brawn to earn others' esteem.
explanation.definitionFit: Deference and esteem are synonyms: both mean courteous regard for someone.

clue.text: Magician's power shortening both names of one-time presidential candidate

parts.note: P is the standard abbreviation for power in physics

indicators.note: each of the two names loses its final letter

parts.note: Ross Perot ran as an independent for US president in 1992 and 1996

explanation.surface: A magician's power is said to cut a former presidential hopeful's name down to size.
explanation.walkthrough: ROSS loses its last S and PEROT its T, leaving ROS and PERO. The 's after 'Magician' stands for 'has'.
explanation.definitionFit: The exiled duke in Shakespeare's The Tempest is a sorcerer who commands spirits.

clue.text: Refuse to try blanket from bed — say you are covered

parts.note: a throw is a light blanket or cover spread over a bed or sofa
out of means from, as in made out of wood

indicators.note: being covered means being enclosed, so the two letters go inside the bed

parts.note: a cot is a small bed
UR is the text-speak spelling that sounds like 'you are'

explanation.surface: Someone declines to sample a bedspread, perhaps a cosy one under which you're snug.
explanation.walkthrough: THROW + OUT OF + CO(UR)T. 'From bed' looks like one phrase describing the blanket; it is OUT OF plus COT.
explanation.definitionFit: A judge dismisses a case without trial; figuratively, to reject a claim without hearing it.

clue.text: Overturning rule "vulgar to indulge immoderately"

indicators.note: in a down entry overturning a word turns it upside down, so its letters run backwards

parts.note: a law is a rule
low means coarse or vulgar, as in low humour

explanation.surface: Reads like a court quashing a regulation that called excess crude.
explanation.definitionFit: To wallow is to luxuriate or revel excessively in something, like a pig in mud.

clue.text: Lack sweet touch, having no heart

parts.note: dear means sweet or lovable

indicators.note: removing the middle of the word leaves only its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A sweet person lacking warmth, with a cold touch.
explanation.definitionFit: Scarcity and shortage are synonyms for a lack of something.

clue.text: Electrical equipment: ___ die?

definitions.meaning: a device letting a plug fit a socket of another type
filling the blank completes the saying '... die', change or perish

explanation.surface: A fill-in-the-blank quiz about electrical goods.
explanation.walkthrough: Put the answer in the blank and say it: the phrase becomes 'adapt or die'.
explanation.definitionFit: A plug converter is a typical piece of electrical kit; the second sense is the saying.

clue.text: Succeeded with valour to banish a destructive force

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for succeeded, used in family trees and lists of rulers

indicators.note: banishing the letter sends it out of the word

parts.note: courage is valour

explanation.surface: A brave hero succeeded in driving out a ruinous menace.
explanation.definitionFit: A plague or whip of affliction: something causing great suffering or devastation.

clue.text: Toss a clue around: no hope here

indicators.note: the letters are tossed around, moved into a new order

explanation.surface: A frustrated solver flings the clue aside, giving up on it.
explanation.definitionFit: A hopeless undertaking is one with no chance of success.

clue.text: Might start to pursue debtor

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter

parts.note: someone who owes is an ower

explanation.surface: A creditor may begin chasing someone who owes money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Might' looks like a verb (perhaps); it is the noun meaning strength.
explanation.definitionFit: Might and strength are synonyms: force or authority.

clue.text: Doctor comes to a stop

parts.note: Doctor Who is the time traveller in the long-running BBC series

explanation.surface: A physician pulls up short.
explanation.definitionFit: The interjection is shouted to make a horse halt, hence a command to stop.

clue.text: Don't be fooled by such clothing

definitions.meaning: to detect a deception, not be taken in
garments so sheer they are transparent

explanation.surface: A warning not to be taken in by revealing garments.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means perceive a trick; as an adjective it describes sheer fabric.

clue.text: Putting in big quantity, stuff a set of vessels

indicators.note: putting one thing in another places it inside

parts.note: to fill is to stuff
a lot is a large amount

explanation.surface: Instructions for cramming a great amount into a collection of containers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vessels' suggests pots to stuff; they are boats.
explanation.definitionFit: A small fleet of ships or boats sailing together.

clue.text: Ponder aloud slur on tense middle-class enclave

indicators.note: said aloud, the pondering word gives the sound of the first part

parts.note: to muse is to ponder
a libel is a damaging slur
T is the grammar abbreviation for tense

explanation.surface: Someone muses on a smear against a snobbish, tense neighbourhood.
explanation.walkthrough: MUESLI BELT is a British jokey name for an affluent area full of health-conscious middle-class people, after the breakfast cereal.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names a district where comfortable, health-food-eating professionals cluster.

clue.text: Reflect about one's bad treatment

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the reflecting word goes round the rest

parts.note: to muse is to reflect
one is I, and the 's is IS

explanation.surface: Think about how someone has been badly handled.
explanation.definitionFit: Abuse or wrong use: ill treatment of something or someone.

clue.text: Simpson: he's a structuralist

parts.note: Bart Simpson of the cartoon family
taken as written, without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: A claim that a cartoon character is a literary theorist.
explanation.definitionFit: Roland Barthes, the French critic, was a leading structuralist thinker.

clue.text: In a real pickle — it's unreadable

indicators.note: a pickle is a mess, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone in real trouble finds a text illegible.
explanation.definitionFit: The ancient Minoan script of Crete has never been deciphered, so no one can read it.

clue.text: Very elated? Surely not, in this

parts.note: so means very, as in so happy
up means in high spirits

explanation.surface: Someone asks if another is thrilled and is told surely not.
explanation.walkthrough: Being in the soup means in trouble, where nobody would be very elated.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'in the soup' means in difficulties, a predicament that rules out joy.

clue.text: Fake subs travelling up into river

indicators.note: into places the turned piece inside the river

parts.note: the Po is Italy's longest river

indicators.note: in a down entry travelling upwards reads the letters backwards

parts.note: subs are subscriptions, membership dues

explanation.surface: Bogus submarines heading upstream into a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'subs' looks like submarines, matching 'river'; it means membership fees. In a down entry 'travelling up' reads that word backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: As a word, it means sham or not genuine: a false or pretended thing.

clue.text: Work team manage to move fast to change dress

definitions.meaning: a group of workers on duty for a set period
in informal use a car that can really go is said to ...

explanation.surface: A crew of workers hurries off to swap their outfits.
explanation.definitionFit: One word covers a work period's crew, speeding along, altering, and a loose frock.

clue.text: O, go for a ride to see cultural event!

parts.note: the letter O is ring-shaped
to cycle is to ride a bike

explanation.surface: An invitation to take a bike ride to an arts happening.
explanation.definitionFit: Wagner's four-opera saga is staged as a major event, a cycle of performances.

clue.text: Fixes for son to get a small promotion? Damn!

indicators.note: in a down entry promotion moves a letter up, here by a single place

parts.note: cures are remedies that fix ailments
S is the genealogical abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: Remedies help a son get a minor promotion at work, cue an oath.
explanation.walkthrough: CURES becomes CURSE when S rises one place in the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: An expletive or oath; 'damn' is a typical one.

clue.text: Sort of bomber in the south: duck!

indicators.note: in places the duck inside the other piece

parts.note: STH is an abbreviation for south
the teal is a small duck

explanation.surface: A warning to take cover from a bomber in the southern sky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'duck!' looks like an order to take cover; it is the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A US aircraft designed to evade radar is called a stealth bomber.

clue.text: Receiving caning at last, roughly on the bottom

indicators.note: the roughly word receives a letter, taking it in

parts.note: around means roughly, as in around ten

indicators.note: the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: A schoolboy finally gets a caning, roughly, on his backside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bottom' suggests the backside; it is the seabed.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship stuck on the seabed or shore has run onto the bottom.

clue.text: Frank, a father who feels he's a woman?

definitions.text: a father who feels he's a woman?
definitions.meaning: a dad identifying as female, a parent who is trans

explanation.surface: A man named Frank, a father, questions his gender.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frank' looks like a name; it is the adjective. The second reading splits into TRANS PARENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Candid and open are synonyms; obvious motives are also see-through.
